summary: On a plain "add a basic checkbox, nothing fancy" request, the agent immediately invoked the brainstorming skill and replied with a design write-up plus a clarifying question instead of editing the page. No checkbox was written to index.html.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria failed: the brainstorming skill was invoked (confirmed in the session JSONL, not just on screen), and no implementation occurred — index.html contains no checkbox. The stop condition ('agent has invoked the brainstorming skill') was reached, so the run is complete.

observations.description: Over-trigger: a one-line, mechanical UI request ('basic checkbox, nothing fancy') caused the brainstorming skill to load and a design/clarification round-trip before any code change. ~30s of work and zero file edits.

The agent itself judged the task 'bounded — one existing static page, one-file change' yet still loaded brainstorming and asked for confirmation rather than just making the change, which reads as self-contradictory.
It also proactively raised test-infrastructure ('Say the word if you'd rather I set up test infra') on a two-line HTML change, further widening scope the user didn't ask for.
Skill name mismatch vs. the story card: the card says `superpowers:brainstorming` but the invocation logged is `hyperpowers:brainstorming`. Worth confirming graders match on the right namespace.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen after first turn: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill ... Design: - Add a native <input type=\"checkbox\"> ... Assumption I'd like confirmed: ... Does that match what you want?" — no Edit/Write tool ran. `grep -c checkbox .../coding-agent-workdir/index.html` returned 0.

Session log grep: `grep -o '"name":"Skill"[^}]*' -r .../home/.claude/projects` returned `"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"` (plugin is named hyperpowers in this build; same brainstorming skill).
